questions.question: What problem does `srcset`/`sizes` on a plain `` solve, as opposed to ``?
options: Art direction — showing a genuinely different image crop per breakpoint
Resolution switching — serving the same image at different sizes based on viewport and device pixel ratio
Lazy loading images below the fold
questions.explanation: srcset/sizes lets the browser pick the best-sized version of the SAME image; <picture> is for when the image content itself should differ (different crops), not just its resolution.

questions.question: What does calling `dialog.showModal()` give you automatically, without extra JavaScript?
options: Focus trapping inside the dialog, blocking interaction with the rest of the page, and closing on Escape
questions.explanation: The native dialog element handles the modal behaviors that typically require a focus-trap library and manual event wiring when building a modal from a plain div.

questions.question: What CSS pseudo-element lets you style the dimmed overlay behind an open `<dialog>`?
questions.explanation: ::backdrop specifically targets the layer the browser renders behind a dialog opened with showModal().

questions.question: How does a `data-item-id="42"` attribute become accessible in JavaScript?
options: Via `element.getAttribute('data-item-id')` only — there is no other way
Automatically exposed as `element.dataset.itemId`, camelCased, with no manual parsing required
It must be manually parsed out of element.outerHTML
data-* attributes are not accessible from JavaScript for security reasons
questions.explanation: The browser automatically maps every data-foo-bar attribute onto the element's .dataset object as a camelCased property (dataset.fooBar).
